participants.name: The rules
participants.description: A Swiss tournament: 16 players and 9 rounds. Each round pairs players on the same score and avoids rematches while it can. No clock.
rules: Every move, the harness sends the model the position, the moves played so far and the list of legal moves, each one described. The model picks one; an LLM answers in JSON limited to those moves.
Since late in round 1, when there is only one legal move it is played without asking the model, which saves time and money.
Two illegal answers in the same game lose it, as in over-the-board chess. Empty or cut-off replies and server errors are asked again and do not count.

From round 8, each move's description also says when it repeats a position or ends the game in a draw: third repetition, stalemate, insufficient material or the fifty-move rule. The history alone was not enough for the models to notice.
Until round 9, a game ended as soon as a third repetition could be claimed; since then, only when it actually happens.
Stockfish judges every game afterwards. Ties in the standings are broken by Buchholz Cut 1, Buchholz, Sonneborn-Berger and wins.

participants.name: Stockfish 19
participants.description: An AI that beats any human in history: the god of chess. In this challenge it would kick every player's ass at 1% of its capacity, so it does not play. It judges every position of every game.

metric.name: Centipawn (cp) loss
metric.text: How many cp, hundredths of a pawn, a move gives away against Stockfish's best move. The evaluation behind it is complex: it weighs material, piece activity, king safety and pawn structure, among other factors, and checks them by searching many moves ahead.

participants.name: Claude Fable 5.1
participants.frontier_note: Anthropic's flagship generally available model; #5 on the LMArena text leaderboard (claude-fable-5.1-max, 1498).
participants.description: Anthropic's top general-purpose Claude model, released in September 2026 as an upgrade to Claude Fable 5. It is best known for agentic coding and long-running knowledge work, and is also the most expensive model in this field.

participants.name: GPT-6 Astra
participants.frontier_note: OpenAI's flagship, which it calls its most intelligent model; #24 on LMArena text so far (gpt-6-astra-max, 1480) on few votes and a wide ±12 interval.
participants.description: OpenAI's flagship GPT-6 model, released to approved users on 3 September 2026 and generally the next day. It is aimed at long end-to-end work such as software engineering, research and computer use, and ties Claude Fable 5.1 as the most expensive model here.

participants.name: Muse Spark 1.3
participants.frontier_note: #8 on the LMArena text leaderboard (muse-spark-1.3-max, 1493); Meta's current top model.
participants.description: Meta's multimodal reasoning model from its Muse Spark line, served through Meta's own API. Version 1.3 focuses on long-running agentic and coding work; Meta has announced an open-weights release of Muse Spark as future roadmap, not for this version.

participants.name: Kimi K3
participants.frontier_note: #17 on LMArena text (kimi-k3-max, 1485), the top-ranked open-weights model, just below the top tier.
participants.description: Moonshot AI's open-weights multimodal reasoning model, described at launch as the largest open-weight language model available. It is known for long-horizon coding and agentic work and a 1-million-token context window.

participants.name: Qwen3.8 Max (0902)
participants.frontier_note: The original Qwen3.8 Max ranks #22 on LMArena text (1481); the 0902 snapshot is not listed separately there.
participants.description: A September 2026 update of Alibaba's largest model, Qwen3.8 Max, with extra training for coding and agentic work. The API model itself is proprietary, but Alibaba published the underlying Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B weights, its first Max-class open release.

participants.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
participants.parameters: 552B MoE, 8B active on input / 16B on output
participants.frontier_note: DeepSeek's low-cost tier; its predecessor V4 Flash ranks #92 on LMArena text and V4.1 Flash has no published rank yet.
participants.description: An open-weights (MIT) model from DeepSeek built on a new encoder-decoder design that activates very few parameters per token, making it very cheap to run. DeepSeek says it beats its larger V4 Pro; it played here with thinking turned off.

participants.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
participants.frontier_note: #9 on the LMArena text leaderboard (gemini-3.8-flash-high, 1493, preliminary), the highest-ranked Google model despite being the cheaper Flash tier.
participants.description: Google's fast, lower-cost Gemini model, released in September 2026 as the third Flash update in about six weeks. It is tuned for coding and agents and approaches the performance of pricier frontier models.

participants.name: Grok 4.7
participants.frontier_note: SpaceXAI's flagship, released two days before this date and not yet on LMArena (its predecessor Grok 4.6 ranks #63), so its standing is unverified.
participants.description: The newest flagship model from SpaceXAI (formerly xAI), released on 21 September 2026 for coding and knowledge work. It is built on a larger base model than Grok 4.6 and trained to check its own work on long tasks.

participants.name: GLM-5.3
participants.frontier_note: #19 on LMArena text (glm-5.3-max, 1483): among the strongest open-weights models, just below the top tier.
participants.description: An open-weights mixture-of-experts model from Z.ai (Zhipu), built on the GLM-5.2 base with improved post-training. Z.ai presents it as the strongest open-weights model for coding and long-horizon agent tasks.

participants.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
participants.frontier_note: Google's frontier reasoning model at its February 2026 release; now #15 on LMArena text (1487), below Google's own Gemini 3.8 Flash.
participants.description: Google's Pro-tier reasoning model, released in preview in February 2026 as an upgrade to Gemini 3 Pro. It is known for strong reasoning (77.1% on ARC-AGI-2 at launch) and multimodal input including audio and video.

participants.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro (0813)
participants.frontier_note: #50 on LMArena text (deepseek-v4-pro-high-20260813, 1463); DeepSeek's large model but well below the top tier.
participants.description: The official, non-preview release of DeepSeek's large V4 Pro mixture-of-experts model, published with open weights under the MIT license. It focuses on agentic coding and tool use; it played here with thinking turned off.

participants.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
participants.frontier_note: The fast, cheap tier of the GPT-5.6 family; #67 on LMArena text (gpt-5.6-luna-xhigh, 1452), and succeeded by GPT-6 Luna on 22 September 2026.
participants.description: The smallest and cheapest member of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, Luna), made for high-volume, low-latency tasks. It can reason at adjustable effort levels despite its low price.

participants.name: Gemma 4 31B
participants.frontier_note: A small open model; #68 on LMArena text (gemma-4-31b, 1451).
participants.description: The largest dense model in Google DeepMind's Gemma 4 family of open models, released under Apache 2.0 and small enough to run on a single workstation GPU. It supports an optional thinking mode, which was not enabled in this tournament.

participants.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
participants.frontier_note: Anthropic's small, fast tier; #129 on LMArena text (1415).
participants.description: Anthropic's smallest and fastest Claude model from October 2025, which matched Claude Sonnet 4 at a fraction of the cost. It is the oldest model in this field and played without extended thinking.

participants.name: Jev
participants.frontier_note: Not a text-generating LLM, so it is not ranked on LMArena; TypeSafe calls it its flagship System One model.
participants.description: TypeSafe AI's first public System One model, launched in early access on 15 September 2026. Instead of writing text, it answers typed questions (choices, scores, yes/no) with calibrated probabilities, typically in well under a second.

participants.name: Human
participants.description: The organiser, playing on the web board against the models, just for fun and to complete the 16 contestants.
